symbols.name: selected chunk count
symbols.meaning: The number of address chunks, at most d, on which the layer acts.
symbols.quote: Here $D$ is a chunk count (not a source group), $e$ counts axes (not digits), and $z$ is an array (not a suffix).

symbols.name: selected axis count
symbols.meaning: The number of selected axes in a group, e = mf.
symbols.quote: Take $e=mf$ selected axes, as $m$ slots of $f$ axes: the selected bits of an address form $f$ columns of $m$ bits.

symbols.name: array
symbols.meaning: An array of records on which the operators act.
symbols.quote: Here $D$ is a chunk count (not a source group), $e$ counts axes (not digits), and $z$ is an array (not a suffix).

symbols.name: basis-change matrix
symbols.meaning: An invertible F_2 matrix whose first columns are the residual basis vectors.
symbols.quote: Let $\Gamma$ be an invertible $\mathbb F_2$-matrix with these $v$ as first columns, and $\mathcal P_\Gamma$ the address permutation moving the value at $x$ to $\Gamma x$.

symbols.name: address permutation
symbols.meaning: The address permutation moving the value at x to Gamma x.
symbols.quote: Let $\Gamma$ be an invertible $\mathbb F_2$-matrix with these $v$ as first columns, and $\mathcal P_\Gamma$ the address permutation moving the value at $x$ to $\Gamma x$.

symbols.name: slot index
symbols.meaning: The index of a slot, matching a residual vector.
symbols.quote: Apply $\mathcal P_\Gamma^{-1}$ to every column, then $(C^{\pm1})^{\otimes f}$ to the $f$ bits of slot $\xi$ for each residual vector $\xi$, then $\mathcal P_\Gamma$: one child on $f=e/m$ axes per residual vector, exactly $s$ in all.

symbols.name: individual chunks
symbols.meaning: The number of leading chunks to which C is applied individually, forming the row index.
symbols.quote: So the first $q_0=\lceil\log_2W\rceil\lceil\log_m(2d)\rceil$ chunks get individual $C$ kernels, in $O(V\log d)$, and their bits form a row index of range $2^{q_0K}\ge W^{\lceil\log_md\rceil}$.

symbols.name: chain operation bound
symbols.meaning: A bound on the number of operations on any chain from an input coefficient to an intermediate value.
symbols.quote: Let $\chi(e)$ bound the operations on any chain from an input coefficient to an intermediate value.

symbols.name: invocation operations
symbols.meaning: A bound on the number of arithmetic operations in one invocation of the network.

symbols.name: level factor
symbols.meaning: The sum s + psi, multiplying a chain bound at each level.
symbols.quote: With $\Psi=s+\psi$, $s\varphi+\psi\le\Psi\varphi$ for any bound $\varphi\ge1$, and there are at most $\lceil\log_md\rceil$ internal levels, so $\chi(e)\le8d\Psi^{\lceil\log_md\rceil+1}\le8\Psi^2d^{\vartheta+1}$, where $\vartheta=\min\{j\ge1:m^j\ge\Psi\}$ is an exponent, not a digit count.

symbols.name: chain bound
symbols.meaning: Any lower bound of at least one on a chain length.
symbols.quote: With $\Psi=s+\psi$, $s\varphi+\psi\le\Psi\varphi$ for any bound $\varphi\ge1$, and there are at most $\lceil\log_md\rceil$ internal levels, so $\chi(e)\le8d\Psi^{\lceil\log_md\rceil+1}\le8\Psi^2d^{\vartheta+1}$, where $\vartheta=\min\{j\ge1:m^j\ge\Psi\}$ is an exponent, not a digit count.

symbols.name: exponent of m
symbols.meaning: The least j at least 1 with m^j at least Psi.
symbols.quote: With $\Psi=s+\psi$, $s\varphi+\psi\le\Psi\varphi$ for any bound $\varphi\ge1$, and there are at most $\lceil\log_md\rceil$ internal levels, so $\chi(e)\le8d\Psi^{\lceil\log_md\rceil+1}\le8\Psi^2d^{\vartheta+1}$, where $\vartheta=\min\{j\ge1:m^j\ge\Psi\}$ is an exponent, not a digit count.

symbols.name: guard constant
symbols.meaning: The constant 128 m Psi^2 in the guard width Delta.
symbols.quote: The pieces and individual kernels keep every chain below $\Delta=\lceil C_0d^{C_1}\rceil$, $C_0=128m\Psi^2$, $C_1=\max\{20,\vartheta+3\}$.
